protocol.name: zext_toplevel_export_v1
protocol.description:
This protocol lets a producer compositor delegate individual toplevel windows — the client's own buffer stream, the full surface tree, and an input back-path — to a consumer compositor, which presents them as first-class windows of its own scene. It is presentation-grade delegation, not screen capture: buffers are the client's original allocations, presentation is paced by the consumer, and the producer retains all shell authority over its clients (serials, grabs, popup placement, activation).
The consumer is an ordinary, privileged Wayland client of the producer. The zext_toplevel_export_manager_v1 global must only be exposed to authorized connections (compositor policy, for example security-context based filtering). Toplevel enumeration through ext-foreign-toplevel-list grants neither export nor input authority, and the producer may deny or revoke the delegation of any surface at any time.
Unless otherwise specified, timestamps are in the producer's CLOCK_MONOTONIC domain, with millisecond timestamps following wl_pointer semantics. Where 64-bit values are carried as two arguments, the value is 'hi' * 0x100000000 + 'lo'. Colour-management and colour-representation state is not carried in version 1 of this protocol.
The key words "must", "must not", "required", "shall", "shall not", "should", "should not", "recommended", "may", and "optional" in this document are to be interpreted as described in IETF RFC 2119.
Warning! The protocol described in this file is currently in the experimental phase. Backward incompatible changes may be added without bumping the major version of the extension. As such, gating usage on the protocol's presence is discouraged outside spatial-os itself.

interface.name: zext_toplevel_export_manager_v1
interface.description: The privileged entry point advertised by the producer. The capabilities event tells the consumer which optional protocol features this producer implements; requests that depend on an absent capability are ignored, and clients should hide or disable the corresponding functionality.

entry.name: already_exported
entry.summary: the toplevel already has an exported tree on this connection

enum.name: capability
enum.description: Optional features of this producer. dmabuf: nodes deliver the client's own dmabuf allocations. input: get_input is honored. pacing: get_pacing is honored. detach_drag: mid-move handoff is honored. dnd: cross-export drag-and-drop (no producer is expected to set this in version 1).

request.name: destroy
request.description: Destroy the manager object. Existing exported trees and their child objects are not affected.

request.name: export_toplevel
request.description: Request export of the toplevel identified by the given ext_foreign_toplevel_handle_v1; identity is always the handle, never title or app-id matching. The producer answers on the returned tree with either node announcements or a denied event. Requesting a second tree for the same toplevel on the same connection raises the already_exported error. If the handle is inert, the returned tree receives denied with the gone reason.

request.name: detach_drag
request.description: Request delegation of the toplevel currently held in the producer's interactive move on the given seat, identified by the producer's active move-grab. The producer ends its move with no placement side-effects (no electric borders, tiling, or output snap) and announces the export on the returned tree, beginning with an anchor event carrying the surface-local cursor-anchor point, so that the consumer's grab can keep the same content pixel under its cursor or ray. If no interactive move is active on the seat when the request is processed — including the race where the move ended in flight — the tree receives denied with the no_active_move reason. Requires the detach_drag capability; without it the request is ignored and the tree is immediately inert.

arg.name: seat
arg.summary: the producer seat whose move-grab is taken over

event.name: capabilities
event.description: The producer's capabilities. Sent once on bind, before any other event on this object.

event.name: main_device
event.description: The DRM device (dev_t, native endianness) client buffers are expected to be allocated on, so the consumer can verify import compatibility before requesting an export. Sent once on bind, after capabilities, and again if the device changes; a change invalidates no existing tree, but subsequent buffers may arrive with a different device.

arg.name: device
arg.summary: dev_t of the producer's main device

interface.name: zext_exported_tree_v1

description.summary: one delegated toplevel and its surface tree

interface.description:
One exported toplevel: the root node, its subsurfaces, and its popups and transients as separate nodes. All node state delivered since the previous done event applies atomically at the next done event.
After a denied event the tree and all its child objects are inert: all requests on them are ignored except the destructors, and no further events referencing them will be sent.

entry.name: pacing_exists
entry.summary: the tree already has a pacing object

entry.name: input_exists
entry.summary: the tree already has an input object

entry.name: invalid_bounds
entry.summary: bounds width or height not positive

enum.name: denied_reason

description.summary: why an export was refused or revoked

enum.description: The typed reason an export was refused, or a live delegation revoked. policy: producer policy (never detailed further, to avoid oracle probing). protected_content: the content is protected. device_mismatch: the consumer cannot import from the buffer device. session_locked: the producer session locked. no_active_move: a detach_drag found no interactive move. gone: the toplevel was closed or the handle was already inert. gpu_reset: the producer lost the device.

entry.name: resume_move
entry.summary: continue the producer's interactive move at the landing point

request.name: destroy
request.description: Stop the delegation. All node, pacing, and input objects become inert. The producer must cancel outstanding input state it created on behalf of this consumer and must release client buffers only after all outstanding consumer release points have signalled or the consumer connection is gone.

request.name: adopt
request.description:
End the delegation, handing the toplevel back to the producer's window-management authority with a landing hint: a producer output (by wl_output reference), coordinates in that output's logical coordinate space, and optionally the resume_move flag, upon which the producer warps its pointer to the landing point and continues its interactive move there, with the final position determined as if an xdg_toplevel move ended at that point. Without resume_move the producer places the toplevel at the hint as a normal placement.
Only delegated toplevels can be adopted; a consumer-native client can never enter the producer's session, since its connection belongs to the consumer. Object lifetime follows destroy: all child objects become inert and buffer teardown follows the destroy rules.

arg.name: output
arg.summary: the producer output to land on

arg.name: x
arg.summary: landing x in the output's logical space

arg.name: y
arg.summary: landing y in the output's logical space

request.name: set_bounds
request.description: Communicate the rectangle, in the root node's surface-local coordinate space, available for popup and transient placement. The producer runs its positioner logic (including reconstraint) against these bounds in place of any output-derived work area: the consumer owns the available volume, the producer owns shell placement. The serial is echoed in the configure_bounds event of placements that used it. Width and height must be positive, otherwise the invalid_bounds error is raised.

arg.name: serial
arg.summary: consumer serial for this bounds update

arg.name: x
arg.summary: bounds x in root surface-local space

arg.name: y
arg.summary: bounds y in root surface-local space

request.name: get_pacing
request.description: Create the pacing object for this tree. A tree has at most one; a second request raises the pacing_exists error. Requires the pacing capability; without it the request is ignored and the returned object is inert.

request.name: get_input
request.description: Create the input back-path object for this tree. A tree has at most one; a second request raises the input_exists error. Requires the input capability; without it the request is ignored and the returned object is inert.

event.name: anchor
event.description: Sent once, before the first done event, on trees created by detach_drag: the root-surface-local position that was under the producer's cursor at handoff, for grab continuity on the consumer side. Never sent on trees created by export_toplevel.

event.name: node
event.description: Announces a node of the exported tree and its parent relation. Nodes are announced parent-first; stacking order within a parent follows the placed_above argument (null means bottom-most among current siblings). Restacking is conveyed by a new node event for an existing node id — consumers must treat it as a stacking update. The node's state arrives through events on the node object and applies at the next done event.

arg.name: parent
arg.summary: parent node, null for the root

arg.name: placed_above
arg.summary: sibling this node stacks directly above, null for bottom-most

event.name: configure_bounds

description.summary: a placement consumed a bounds update

event.description: The producer placed or reconstrained a popup against the bounds identified by the echoed serial. Lets the consumer correlate popup geometry changes with its own bounds updates.

arg.name: serial
arg.summary: the set_bounds serial that was used

event.name: denied
event.description: The export was refused, or a live delegation revoked. The tree and all child objects are inert from this event on. The producer has already cancelled consumer-originated input state and will release client buffers only once outstanding fenced GPU work completes.

event.name: done
event.description: All node state (buffers, damage, geometry, regions) delivered since the previous done event applies atomically now. This allows changes to the tree to be seen as atomic, even if they happen via multiple events. The commit id identifies this state for presentation feedback; ids increase monotonically per tree.

interface.name: zext_exported_node_v1

description.summary: one surface in the exported tree

interface.description:
One surface of the exported tree, mirroring the client's commits. Buffers are announced as zext_exported_buffer_v1 objects and attached by reference; all state applies at the tree's next done event.
When the underlying surface is unmapped or the tree becomes inert, the node is inert: requests other than the destructor are ignored and no further events reference it.

enum.name: fallback_kind
enum.description: Delegated zero-copy delivery is unavailable for this node. shm_only: the client commits wl_shm buffers. device_mismatch: the consumer cannot import from this buffer's device. protected_content: the buffer is protected. Consumers are expected to present such nodes through a capture-based profile instead; this protocol never falls back to silent copies.

request.name: destroy
request.description: Destroy the node object. Buffer objects announced through it are not affected; their leases end through their own release and retired semantics.

event.name: buffer
event.description: A buffer entered the node's active set: the client's original allocation, leased to the consumer for sampling. Format is a DRM fourcc; the modifier is hi/lo combined. Plane events follow on the buffer object, one per plane. The producer enforces its negotiated in-flight cap by revoking (denied on the tree) rather than by blocking its client.

arg.name: modifier_hi
arg.summary: upper 32 bits of the format modifier

arg.name: modifier_lo
arg.summary: lower 32 bits of the format modifier

event.name: attach

description.summary: buffer attached for the next done, with acquire point

event.description: The named buffer is the node's content from the next done event on. The acquire argument carries a DRM syncobj timeline fd; the consumer must not sample the buffer before the acquire point signals. Each attach obligates the consumer to exactly one release on the buffer object once its reads complete.

arg.name: point_hi
arg.summary: upper 32 bits of the acquire point

arg.name: point_lo
arg.summary: lower 32 bits of the acquire point

event.name: damage

description.summary: damage since the previous attach of this buffer

event.description: One damage rectangle in buffer coordinates; sent zero or more times before the done event that applies the attach.

event.name: position
event.description: The node's offset in its parent's surface-local coordinate space. For the root node this event is never sent; the consumer owns the root's placement.

event.name: scale
event.description: The client's buffer scale and output transform for this surface, with transform values as in wl_output.transform.

event.name: viewport
event.description: The surface's wp_viewport state: source rectangle in buffer coordinates (all -1 if unset) and destination size in surface-local coordinates (both -1 if unset).

event.name: geometry
event.description: The xdg-surface window geometry of this node in surface-local coordinates: the part of the surface the consumer should treat as the window, excluding client-side shadows.

event.name: region_rect

description.summary: one rectangle of a pending region

event.description: One rectangle, surface-local, of the region being replaced; the rectangles accumulate until region_done and replace the previous region of that kind at the next done event.

description.summary: the pending region of this kind is complete

event.name: fallback
event.description: Zero-copy delivery is not available for this node, for the given typed reason. No buffer or attach events will be sent for it.

event.name: unmapped
event.description: The underlying surface was unmapped. The node is inert; outstanding buffer leases still require their releases.

interface.name: zext_exported_buffer_v1
interface.description: One client buffer leased to the consumer. Plane events describe the dmabuf; each attach on the owning node obligates exactly one release. The producer joins the consumer's release point with its own completion before releasing the buffer to its client; the consumer never touches the client's release timeline. Releases may complete out of order across buffers.

entry.name: excess_release
entry.summary: release sent without a matching outstanding attach

request.name: destroy
request.description: Destroy the buffer object. If attaches are outstanding, the producer must treat the lease as ended only when the consumer connection's outstanding release points signal or the connection is gone; a consumer should send its releases before destroying the object.

request.name: release
request.description: Return one outstanding attach of this buffer: the release argument carries a DRM syncobj timeline fd whose given point the consumer signals when its reads of the buffer complete. Sending more releases than there are outstanding attaches raises the excess_release error.

arg.name: point_hi
arg.summary: upper 32 bits of the release point

arg.name: point_lo
arg.summary: lower 32 bits of the release point

event.name: plane
event.description: One plane of the buffer, in plane-index order; num_planes such events follow the announcing buffer event.

event.name: retired
event.description: The client freed or replaced this buffer; it will not be attached again. The object is inert once all outstanding attaches are released; the consumer should then destroy it.

interface.name: zext_export_pacing_v1
interface.description: Consumer-driven pacing for one exported tree. While this object exists and a clock has been set, the producer dispatches the tree's client frame callbacks against the consumer's cadence instead of its own outputs'; destroying the object atomically returns the tree to producer-paced mode. Exactly one pacing mode owns a tree at any time.

enum.name: presented_flags
enum.description: zero_copy means the consumer scanned out or sampled the client's buffer directly in its final presentation path. It must never be set merely because no intermediate allocation existed on the wire.

request.name: destroy

description.summary: return the tree to producer pacing

request.description: Destroy the pacing object. The tree atomically returns to producer-paced frame callback dispatch; no presented or discarded events follow.

request.name: set_consumer_clock
request.description: Supply the consumer's presentation clock (a CLOCK_* id valid for clock_gettime) and correlation to the producer's CLOCK_MONOTONIC: a pair of timestamps sampled together, so the producer can convert frame arguments into its own domain. May be sent again to refine the correlation.

request.name: frame
request.description: One upcoming consumer frame: predicted display time (consumer clock, nanoseconds, hi/lo), the frame period, and the commit cutoff before display time by which tree state must be done to be sampled. The producer schedules the tree's client frame callbacks so commits land before the cutoff. Sending frame before set_consumer_clock raises the no_clock error.

arg.name: display_time_hi
arg.summary: upper 32 bits of predicted display ns

arg.name: display_time_lo
arg.summary: lower 32 bits of predicted display ns

arg.name: cutoff_ns
arg.summary: commit cutoff before display time, ns

event.name: presented
event.description: The consumer first sampled the tree state identified by commit_id at the given time (consumer clock, nanoseconds, hi/lo). Sent by the producer on the consumer's report; exactly one of presented or discarded is sent per commit id while consumer-paced.

arg.name: time_hi
arg.summary: upper 32 bits of sample time ns

arg.name: time_lo
arg.summary: lower 32 bits of sample time ns

event.name: discarded
event.description: The tree state identified by commit_id was never sampled — a newer state replaced it first, or it missed its cutoff and the consumer reused the last ready state.

interface.name: zext_export_input_v1
interface.description:
The input back-path for one exported tree. Requests address tree nodes in surface-local coordinates; the producer translates them into its own protocol streams towards its client, generating its own wire serials and owning implicit grabs, popup dismissal, and focus. Requests naming an inert node are ignored. Drag-and-drop is absent in version 1; producers advertise it with the dnd capability when a future version adds it.
Pointer and touch requests accumulate and are delivered to the producer's client at the frame requests, following wl_pointer and wl_touch frame semantics. Timestamps are milliseconds in the producer's CLOCK_MONOTONIC domain; the consumer converts using the pacing clock correlation, or sends its own monotonic milliseconds if no pacing object exists.

request.name: destroy
request.description: Destroy the input object. The producer cancels consumer-originated pointer, keyboard, and touch state towards its client (leave events, key releases, touch cancel).

request.name: pointer_button
request.description: Button codes and state values follow wl_pointer.button semantics.

request.name: pointer_axis
request.description: Axis values follow wl_pointer.axis semantics; high-resolution discrete steps accompany as pointer_axis_value120 within the same frame.

request.name: pointer_axis_value120
request.description: Discrete axis movement in fractions of 120, following wl_pointer.axis_value120 semantics.

description.summary: end of a logical pointer event group

request.name: keyboard_key
request.description: Key codes are in the keymap announced by the keymap event; the producer computes and delivers modifier state to its client itself.

arg.name: key
arg.summary: key code in the announced keymap

description.summary: touch point down on a node
end of a logical touch event group

request.name: activate
request.description: The consumer's user performed an activating gesture on the node. This never carries a foreign xdg-activation token: the producer mints and validates its own token from this intent, subject to its focus-stealing policy.

entry.name: pointer_grab
entry.summary: an implicit or popup pointer grab

event.name: keymap

description.summary: the keymap key codes are interpreted in

event.description: The keymap the producer's client receives; keyboard_key codes must be valid in it. Sent before the first keyboard_key may be sent, and again whenever the producer's keymap changes.

event.name: focus
event.description: Reports where the producer's focus or an active grab of the given kind sits within this tree, or null when it left the tree. Purely informational: the producer owns the state.

event.name: popup_dismissed
event.description: The producer broke a popup grab (for example on an outside click it synthesized, or its own policy). The consumer should stop presenting the node; the unmapped event on the node follows.
